meta.title: Persian B2 Upper Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Persian → English (see the Persian, recall the meaning) and English → Persian (see an English meaning, recall the Persian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an upper-intermediate learner, aligned to B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics, including technical discussions in their field of specialisation' — a learner here is able to interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible without strain for either party, and to produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects and explain a viewpoint on a topical issue, giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. The Persian taught is the standard written language of Iran (Farsi), with the everyday spoken form shown beside a word where Tehran speech says it differently. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Persian, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 106 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — politics and public administration, the law and the courts, the economy and finance, science and research, technology, the environment and natural resources, health and the mind, the arts, literature, calligraphy and the media, history and society, argument and evaluation — the words for claims, evidence, causes and consequences — the formal connectors of written Persian, and the verbs of reporting, analysing and persuading — and the other 1394 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Persian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb, and its spoken form, added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in the Persian script with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's Iranian one (â for the long a, x for kh, š for sh: ketâb, xâne), since the script writes no short vowels; the Persian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 1098 nouns show their plural; the 44 verbs show their present stem, which no rule derives from the infinitive and on which every present tense is built, and behind the All forms fold their present, past, future, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 742 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 201 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
